FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.

2. When practising Oral expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral expression.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral expression.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expression.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.

3. When practising Grammar, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar.

4. When practising Persuasive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive speaking.

5. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Good morning / hello
   C. Good night only
   D. Thank you

6. When practising Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Comprehension.

7. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.

8. When practising Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.

9. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. livre
   B. fenêtre
   C. porte
   D. chaise

10. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.

11. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.

12. When practising Listening for Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Vocabulary.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Oral expression and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive speaking.

5. B — Good morning / hello

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.

9. A — livre

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

11. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Vocabulary.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral expression; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
